transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what finally got me to come in is... I keep arranging my whole day so I don’t have to drive over these high bridges. Like I’ll take a longer route, leave earlier, that kind of thing. And I know it probably sounds silly, because I’ve driven for years—used to drive all over for work, and the roads are worse now anyway, don’t get me started on that—but if I can’t avoid one of those bridges, I’m gripping the wheel the whole time, just trying to get across.
Do you find yourself avoiding other things or situations besides high bridges because of anxiety or fear?

Not really other things, no. It’s mostly those high bridges. I mean, I’ll plan my whole day around not having to drive over them—take some ridiculous longer way, even if traffic’s worse, and traffic’s always worse lately—but if I can’t avoid it, I just grip the wheel and kind of force myself across.
